chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan Za'lan, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn al-Tayyar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Hajj performed in succession, and Umra performed constantly, both dispel the abject poverty and the evil death'.

key_terms.تَتْرَى: In succession or one after another
key_terms.حِجَجٌ: Plural of Hajj, referring to multiple pilgrimages
key_terms.عُمَرٌ: Plural of Umra, referring to multiple minor pilgrimages
key_terms.مِيتَةَ السَّوْءِ: Evil death or death in a state of hardship/sin

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and material benefits of performing Hajj and Umra frequently according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual and material efficacy of frequent pilgrimage, noting that persistent Hajj and Umra act as divine safeguards against poverty (ailat al-faqar) and ensure a blessed end to life (mitat as-saw'). This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of worship as both a means of sustenance and a preparation for the transition to the afterlife, emphasizing the transformative power of consistent devotion.
